task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: offensive reorganization relative to baseline L (undefined in the question)
methodological_questions: How is 'offensive reorganization relative to L' defined and measured reliably from play-by-play-derived play-type records?
What is the unit (spell, player-absence event, team-game) and the PPP change window, and what minimum detectable effect (rho) applies to n=148 spells?
Does reorganization predict change in PPP after controlling for usage, rotation changes, opponent quality, and season type?
Can player absences be identified without selection on the outcome (regression to the mean)?

historical_evidence.finding: Pre-registered test on 23 player-season absences from 18 franchises. V1 (real absences move the association structure) was confirmed (16/23 above own-null p95, binomial p=2.67e-16; V1(b) +0.142, CI [+0.103, +0.187]). V2 (simulation predicts magnitude) was not confirmed (Spearman +0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667]). Record notes franchises below the registered floor of about 20 and that a later full-pool run reversed V2.

Live trigger timing study in playoff replays (101 to 228 triggers). Early vs late BEST-AVOID gap (0.701 vs 0.415) rests on 26 early triggers. BEST vs AVOID p=0.073965 in the 10-series replay, confirmed in the 25-series replay per [prior work]. One record calls its p=0.031 (n=57) weak evidence. Spearman tier vs ROG PPP rho=-0.0457, p=0.456, n=268.
Compared V4 and V5 player routing on observed PPP. 8 divergences, 0 scoreable; players missing from Neo4j and V5 mostly routed to 'team'. No hit rate recorded.

Scanned 6,221 (offense, opponent, play type) cells. The apparent +1.26 PPP [source] (n>=5) and +1.13 (n>=15) came from low-n cells, e.g. 1-shot role players at 3.00 PPP. Record attributes the [source] to small-sample inflation and recommends keeping the n>=15 gate.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player-level PPP comparison from Neo4j-derived routing records
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable: players were missing from [source] and routing defaulted to 'team', so 0 of 8 divergences were scoreable. Coverage was not checked before running.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Cell-level PPP leader/matchup signal from small-possession cells
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: the apparent effect was small-sample inflation in cells with few possessions (n=5-9), dominated by 1-shot role players.
Recorded as underpowered: franchise count below the registered floor of about 20 (auto_limited_by [prior work]). Record notes a later full-pool run reversed V2.
Recorded as inconclusive: the early-vs-late gap rests on 26 early triggers, and the p=0.031 result is called weak evidence.

evidence_establishes: Earlier studies by this project on related absence and playoff-trigger questions were underpowered or ended inconclusive, untestable, or artifact, so small-n contrasts in this data have a poor track record.
Player-level joins from [source] have had coverage gaps ([prior work][prior work]), so the derived records need a coverage check before use.
Absence-based structural shifts are detectable in some settings (FAM:[prior work] V1), but this does not test the magnitude of PPP change.
No retrieved record tests reorganization relative to L predicting change in PPP. Prior work on this exact question is not present in the retrieval.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether reorganization relative to L predicts change in PPP; no retrieved record measures this.
The meaning of 'relative to L' or the change-in-PPP window; neither is defined in the question or [prior work].
An achievable MDE for the 148-spell design; the data description gives 'mde rho' without a value.
Whether the 2025-26 playoff data (complete from 2026-06-21) or the regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) is comparable across seasons.
Any effect size, direction, or reliability estimate for reorganization metrics.
own_inferences: The question as posed is underspecified (undefined L, undefined reorganization metric, undefined outcome window), so it cannot be tested as stated.
With 148 spells, a modest rho is likely to be underpowered, and multiple reorganization metrics or windows would inflate false positives.
Absence events are selected on injury and minutes, which creates regression-to-the-mean and selection risk in any PPP change measure.
Play-type initiator labels derived from play-by-play may carry systematic labelling error that could drive the reorganization measure.
uncertainties: The unit of 'n=986' versus '148 spells' is ambiguous; [prior work] does not say which is the analysis unit.
No MDE value is given for rho, so achievable power cannot be computed.
Reliability of the reorganization measure across games is unknown.
Whether the Neo4j player coverage problem in [prior work][prior work] also affects the play-type records used here is unknown.
Retrieval returned no record directly on reorganization, L, or PPP change after absence.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records are about adjacent questions (trigger timing, absence structure, routing, cell-level leaders), not this question. They do not establish feasibility. They do show a repeated pattern in this project of small-n contrasts ending as inconclusive, untestable, or artifact ([prior work], [prior work], SF-[prior work], [prior work]). That pattern, together with the undefined terms in the question, moved the decision from a provisional proceed to do_not_proceed until the definitions and power are fixed.

blocking_constraints.text: 'Reorganization relative to L' has no operational definition, and its reliability from play-type records is unknown.
148 spells with an unspecified MDE rho may be underpowered; [prior work] family shows small-sample failures.
Reorganization is derived from play-by-play play-type labels, which may be outcome-dependent if points are used in the labelling.
Absences are selected on injury and minutes, so PPP change after absence is confounded with regression to the mean.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests reorganization relative to L predicting change in PPP. The cited records cover adjacent questions. They supply design lessons (small-n artifacts, coverage gaps, underpowered absence pools) but no answer to the question.

risks.text: Undefined L and reorganization metric; reliability across games and seasons not established.
148 spells and unknown MDE rho; the historical records show small-sample failures (FAM:[prior work], FAM:[prior work], FAM:[prior work]).
Absence-spell exposures may be sparse for specific players or lineups, leaving thin cells.
Play-type initiator labels derived from play-by-play may depend on the points outcome they are used to predict.
Play-type and initiator attribution from play-by-play can be misassigned.
Usage, rotation changes, opponent quality, and playoff vs regular season may drive both reorganization and PPP change.
Absence events are selected on injury and minutes; PPP change may reflect regression to the mean.
Player-level joins in [source] have dropped players ([prior work][prior work]), which could silently bias spell assignment.
Season and playoff periods differ, and 2025-26 playoffs are partial before 2026-06-21, so pooling may mix regimes.
Multiple reorganization metrics, windows, or L definitions would inflate false positives.

design.estimand: Association between a pre-specified reorganization metric (relative to a defined baseline L) and the change in PPP in the window after a player absence spell, with L and the window fixed before analysis.
design.unit: Absence spell (player-absence event by team), with team-game PPP before and after as the outcome. Use the derived play-type records only after a coverage check.
design.sample: Only after definitions are fixed: confirm the spell count (148 versus 986 units) and report the coverage of player IDs in [source]. Pool regular seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 and playoffs separately; the 2025-26 playoffs are used only from 2026-06-21, when they are complete.
design.power: Compute the MDE rho for the actual spell count before running. If MDE exceeds a pre-registered effect size of interest, do not run the test; report it as underpowered.
design.controls: Usage, minutes share, rotation-change indicators, opponent defensive rating, season type, and a team fixed effect. Use the reliability of the reorganization metric (split-half across games) as a covariate or attenuation check.
design.falsification: A placebo window before the absence, and a non-absence matched spell set. A reorganization effect that also appears pre-absence is treated as artifact.
design.multiplicity: One primary metric and one primary window, fixed in advance. Other metrics or windows are exploratory and labelled as such, with Holm correction for any secondary claims.
design.decision_rule: Support requires the pre-specified primary estimate to clear its pre-registered threshold with a CI excluding zero, a placebo window showing no effect, and the reliability check passing. Otherwise report uncertain, or rejected only if the design is adequately powered for the effect of interest.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 through 2025-26, regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21; data as of 2026-11-01.
